_provenance.note: New Mexico citation authorities. New Mexico's operative SNAP regulation is NMAC (New Mexico Administrative Code) Title 8, Chapter 139 ("Food Stamp Program"), a dedicated SNAP-only chapter (unlike Connecticut's shared multi-program UPM), cited by a 'Title.Chapter.Part.Section' pattern, e.g. '8.139.420.8 NMAC'. This pack ALSO cites a real, separate New Mexico statute (N.M. Stat. Ann. § 27-2B-11) for the drug-felony finding, so this pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'NMSA 27-2B-', matching this roster's Connecticut, Kentucky, Alabama, and Louisiana packs' multi-family pattern.

patterns.note: New Mexico Administrative Code, Title 8 (Social Services), Chapter 139 (Food Stamp Program), cited by Title.Chapter.Part.Section, e.g. 8.139.420.8 (Categorical Eligibility), 8.139.510 (Resources and Property), 8.139.520 (Income and Deductions), 8.139.120.8 (Recertification).

New Mexico Statutes Annotated, Chapter 27 (Public Assistance), Article 2B (New Mexico Works Act), cited by section number. This pack cites exactly one: § 27-2B-11(C), the drug-felony SNAP/TANF eligibility opt-out provision.

nmac.note: Recipient Policy — Who Can Be a Recipient (household composition, basis for defining group); hsd.state.nm.us-hosted PDF still shows pre-2024 HSD issuing-agency line
General Recipient Requirements — Nonfinancial Eligibility Criteria (SSN enumeration, general work requirements); hsd.state.nm.us-hosted PDF still shows pre-2024 HSD issuing-agency line
General Recipient Requirements — Categorical Eligibility (CE); amended 7/16/2024, further amended 3/1/2025; 8.139.420.8 is the operative broad-based CE section, 200% FPG threshold
Eligibility Policy — Resources and Property; effective 7/16/2024; defers to USDA's own COLA page for the current dollar-figure resource limit rather than restating it

Eligibility Policy — Income and Deductions; amended 7/1/2024; states the 130%/100% FPG gross/net structure and the CE income-test distinction (financial-assistance CE skips both tests, broad-based CE must still meet both)
Recertification — timely-reapplication rule (15th day of the certification period's last month) for uninterrupted benefits

nmsa.note: New Mexico Works Act — ineligibility grounds for public assistance; subsection (C) is New Mexico's drug-felony SNAP/TANF opt-out, invoking 21 U.S.C. § 862a(d)(1)(A) but narrowly scoped in its own text to convictions for DISTRIBUTION of a controlled substance — this pack could not confirm, and flags as genuinely ambiguous, whether the exemption extends to possession/use convictions. Could not be fetched directly (law.justia.com 403, nmonesource.com 404); sourced via two independently-fetched, textually-convergent mirrors (Public Health Law Center, FindLaw), see PROVENANCE.md
